rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The Lorentz force is the electric force plus the magnetic force. In crossed fields the forces cancel at v = E/B, which is the speed a velocity selector passes. A later magnetic field bends that beam into a circle whose radius gives m/q.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
F = qvB sinθ
ε = −N dΦ/dt
F = BIL

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Crossed fields mean E, B and v are mutually perpendicular.  ·  The cyclotron frequency is q B /(2 π m).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: The Lorentz force is the total electromagnetic force on a charge, q E plus the magnetic force q v B. The electric part can speed the charge up. The magnetic part only turns it.  ·  If E and B are perpendicular to each other and to the velocity, the two forces can point in opposite directions. They cancel when q E = q v B, so v = E/B.

rows.label: Limitation

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Lorentz force  ·  Velocity selector  ·  Mass spectrometer  ·  Cyclotron frequency

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: • Motion of charged particles in magnetic fields  ·  Electric force is q E.  ·  Magnetic force is q v B.  ·  They can be set opposite.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Force on moving charge F = q(v×B); on a wire F = BIL sinθ.  ·  Faraday: EMF ε = −dΦ/dt; Lenz's law gives the sign (induced current opposes the change in flux).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: What is the cyclotron frequency?

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: A velocity selector has E = 2.0 × 10^4 V/m and B = 0.20 T, crossed so the forces oppose. Find the speed that goes straight through.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The Lorentz force includes → B  ·  In a velocity selector, v equals → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A velocity selector is a pair of crossed fields. Charges of the chosen speed go straight through. Faster charges are bent one way and slower charges the other way. The charge and the mass cancel, so the selected speed does not depend on them.  ·  After the selector, a magnetic field alone bends the beam into a circle whose radius is m v / (q B). Measuring that radius at the known speed gives the mass-to-charge ratio.  ·  A cyclotron uses the magnetic circle and an electric kick twice per revolution to increase the speed. The frequency of the orbit for a non-relativistic particle is q B / (2 π m), independent of the speed.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: L = NΦ/I  ·  The selected speed is E/B.  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ..

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The selector condition is v = E/B, not E B.  ·  The magnetic force still does no work.  ·  The selected speed does not depend on q or m.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The cyclotron frequency does depend on q, m and B.  ·  Set the forces opposite before equating them.  ·  Do not use the selector formula when E and B are parallel.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Write F = q E + q v B and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.  ·  Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Self-inductance L = NΦ/I; inductance stores energy U = ½LI². Mutual inductance M couples two coils.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  Limit to remember: force on moving charge f = q(v×b); on a wire f = bil sinθ.
